newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam prints photo of firing squad execution.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam prints photo of firing squad execution.

text.p: Vietnam published a rare photograph on Saturday of a firing squad execution of a man convicted of the brutal killing of a nine-year-old girl.
The photo, in the People's Police newspaper, showed Le Hong Bich tied to a post and standing in a shallow hole in a field before a firing squad.
The picture, apparently taken only moments before the squad opened fire, was indistinct. In the background was what appeared to be a large crowd of people.
The newspaper said Bich had been found guilty of killing the girl in April last year by strangling her with a towel, removing jewellery and raping her before dumping the body in a river.
He later sold the jewellery for $50.

Publication of such a photo is extremely rare in Vietnam and is believed to be unprecedented in recent years. Although death sentences are reported by state media, mention of actual execution is less common.
The newspaper said the sentence was carried out on August 25 and took place in An Giang province on Vietnam's southern border with Cambodia.
